justification: The run delivered a substantial, generally competent opening package on storeys 2 and 3 and windows throughout, but the entire occupied ground floor remains without doors or an exterior entrance. Under the doors and windows standard, a whole use group/storey with no access is Blocking, so the result cannot score above 5 despite the sound upper-floor work.
evidence: Live measurements found 178 openings: storey 1 has 0 doors and 35 windows, storey 2 has 37 doors and 34 windows, and storey 3 has 37 doors and 35 windows. The access check reported 112 rooms total, including 38 ground-floor rooms with no door; the agent accurately disclosed: “The ground floor has its 35 windows but none of its 51 doors yet.”
strengths: All 178 delivered openings are hosted in walls; no unhosted openings were measured.
Storeys 2 and 3 each have doors serving all 37 rooms, with coherent room-to-circulation topology.
The automatic checks and a new opening check found no swing, hinge, width, lift-door, or sash-rule findings among the delivered openings.
Single room doors measure 1.00 m nominal and 0.86 m clear after repair; double doors measure about 1.94 m nominal, while lift landing doors are sliding and 1.20 m wide.
The two lift reservations on each upper floor use the “Lift Landing Door – Centre Opening” family, version 1, opening onto shared lift lobbies.
Upper stair-reservation doors use “Pair Flush Door,” version 5, with a 60-minute fire rating; opening measurements show they open into the stair reservations.
All 104 windows face outside and are hosted. Their measured width is about 2.413 m, height about 1.813 m, with consistent approximately 0.894 m sill height relative to each storey.
The agent was candid about the incomplete ground floor and did not claim whole-building access was complete.
weaknesses: Blocking: all 38 occupied ground-floor rooms have no door, including offices, waiting areas, retail, café seating, passenger support rooms, service rooms, circulation spaces, and both reserved stair zones.
There is no ground-floor exterior entrance or final exit door, so the transport terminal cannot be entered or used as delivered.
The opening task is incomplete across the building: the agent described 51 planned ground-floor doors but delivered none of them.

Whole-building reachability remains unverified; the live access result is "unverified" with 38 no-door rooms and 74 upper-floor rooms reported as not linked to other floors because no valid ground entrance exists.
Moving-leaf collision sweeps and a complete clash check were not established, so those aspects are not assessed rather than passed.

spec_violations.constraint: Add doors and windows to this transport-terminal as a whole-building task.
spec_violations.what_happened: Windows were added throughout and doors were added only on storeys 2 and 3; the entire occupied ground floor has no doors.
spec_violations.evidence: Live opening counts are storey 1: 0 doors/35 windows; storey 2: 37/34; storey 3: 37/35. The access check reports 38 ground-floor rooms with no door.

spec_violations.constraint: Every occupied storey and room-use group must have door coverage and room-to-circulation access.
spec_violations.what_happened: Ground-floor public, controlled, service, circulation, lift-reservation, and stair-reservation spaces all lack doors.
spec_violations.evidence: The access check summary: 112 rooms, 38 with no door; no room on the ground floor has a door.

spec_violations.constraint: The building must have a usable public entrance and appropriate exits.
spec_violations.what_happened: No delivered ground-floor door connects the terminal to outside.
spec_violations.evidence: The opening check found zero doors on storey 1 and no outside-facing doors anywhere in the delivered set.
